name: Data representation scatter graphs and correlation

questions.q: Which type of correlation is expected between the age of a used car and its resale price?
What does a scatter graph primarily allow you to investigate?
a: The exact mean of a single dataset
The relationship between two different variables
The frequency distribution of grouped data
The probability of an independent event

questions.q: If points on a scatter graph trend upward from left to right as one variable increases while the other decreases, what type of relationship is shown?
When drawing a line of best fit on a scatter graph, what is the primary rule to follow?
a: It must connect the first and last data points directly
It should have a roughly even balance of points above and below the line
It must pass through the origin (0, 0)
It should connect the maximum number of exact points possible

questions.q: What term describes estimating a value inside the range of data collected on a scatter graph?
What term describes estimating a value outside the range of data collected on a scatter graph?
Why is extrapolation generally less reliable than interpolation?
a: It assumes the established trend continues indefinitely beyond known data
It requires the line of best fit to be curved
It only applies to categorical variables

questions.q: If points on a scatter graph are scattered completely randomly with no discernible pattern, what can be concluded?
a: There is no correlation between the variables

questions.q: Which of the following pairs of variables is most likely to show positive correlation?
a: Hours spent revising for a math test and the exam score achieved
Speed of a car and the time taken to complete a fixed journey
Age of a dog and its running speed

questions.q: Which of the following pairs of variables is most likely to show negative correlation?
a: Height of a person and their shoe size
Number of people in a household and weekly grocery cost
Amount of fuel left in a car tank and distance travelled since last fill

questions.q: What does a strong correlation coefficient indicate about data points on a scatter graph?
a: They are tightly clustered close to the line of best fit
They form a perfectly horizontal line
They are randomly spread across the entire grid
They have equal mean and median values

questions.q: In a scatter graph analyzing study time versus test scores, what does an outlier represent?
a: The most common result in the class
A data point that does not fit the overall trend of the rest of the data
The exact midpoint of the data set
An error in the axis labels

questions.q: If a scatter graph shows that as advertising budget increases, sales revenue also increases at a steady rate, how would you describe the correlation?
Which of the following statements about correlation and causation is correct?
a: Correlation always proves that one variable causes the other
Correlation means two variables move together, but it does not automatically prove causation
Causation can only exist if correlation is exactly zero
Correlation and causation mean the exact same thing in statistics

questions.q: When plotting a scatter graph, which axis is traditionally used for the independent variable?
When plotting a scatter graph, which axis is traditionally used for the dependent variable?
If a line of best fit passes through the points (2, 4) and (6, 12), what is its gradient?
What does a correlation value close to negative one (-1) signify?
What does a correlation value close to positive one (+1) signify?
If a scatter graph displays data points forming a curved U-shape, what type of relationship is present?
Which tool is best suited for identifying trends or relationships between two continuous numerical variables?

What can cause an outlier on a scatter graph?
a: An experimental error, a recording mistake, or an exceptional individual case

questions.q: Which of the following describes a moderate negative correlation?
a: Points trend downwards from left to right, with some spread around the line
Points trend upwards from left to right tightly packed
Points form a horizontal straight line
Points form a vertical straight line

questions.q: In an experiment measuring temperature and ice cream sales, what is the independent variable?
a: The colour of the shop sign

questions.q: In an experiment measuring temperature and ice cream sales, what is the dependent variable?
If the equation of a line of best fit is y = 3x + 5, what is the expected value of y when x = 4?
If the equation of a line of best fit is y = -2x + 20, what is the expected value of y when x = 5?
Why should a line of best fit not be forced to pass through the origin (0, 0) unless justified by context?
a: It can distort the true relationship shown by the data points
It makes the gradient impossible to calculate
It turns the scatter graph into a bar chart

questions.q: What does a cluster of data points separate from the main group on a scatter graph indicate?
a: A calculation error in the mean
A distinct sub-group or a unique cluster within the population

questions.q: Which statement is true regarding data points and a line of best fit?
a: Every single data point must lie directly on the line of best fit
The line of best fit represents the overall trend and rarely touches every single point
The line of best fit must connect the highest and lowest points
Data points are drawn after the line is finalised without real values

questions.q: If two variables have a correlation of zero, what does their scatter graph look like?
a: A random scatter of points with no obvious upward or downward trend

questions.q: When is a scatter graph NOT appropriate for displaying data?
a: When comparing category names (like eye color) against a single numerical variable
When investigating test scores against hours of sleep

questions.q: If the gradient of a line of best fit is negative, what does this indicate about the correlation?
If the gradient of a line of best fit is positive, what does this indicate about the correlation?
What is the primary risk of relying on extrapolation?
a: Conditions may change outside the tested range, making the prediction inaccurate
It takes too long to calculate manually
It changes the original data points on the graph

questions.q: How can you make predictions more accurate when using a line of best fit?
a: By guessing a value without looking at the line
By using interpolation within a large, densely populated dataset
By ignoring outliers completely without checking them
By drawing the line as steep as possible

questions.q: Which of these variables would show NO correlation when plotted on a scatter graph?
a: Shoe size and math test score
Age of a house and its market value

questions.q: What is the main purpose of a scatter graph in statistical analysis?
a: To display frequencies of single categorical groups
To visually assess whether a relationship exists between two numerical variables
To show changes in a single variable over time
